settings.label: Region
settings.meaning: The AWS Region the user pool is in, such as us-east-1. It names the host every call goes to and the tokens' issuer.
settings.whereToFind: The first part of the user pool ID (us-east-1 in us-east-1_EXAMPLE), or the Region selector in the Amazon Cognito console.

settings.label: User pool ID
settings.meaning: The user pool the app's users live in. Tokens are checked against its keys and issuer. Test and production use separate user pools.
settings.whereToFind: Amazon Cognito console › User pools › the pool › Overview, User pool ID. Use a separate user pool for test.

settings.label: App client ID
settings.meaning: The app client users sign in through. ID tokens carry it as aud and access tokens as client_id.
settings.whereToFind: The user pool › App clients › the app client, Client ID.

settings.label: App client secret
settings.meaning: Only for a confidential app client (one with a secret): sent on token requests and in the SECRET_HASH of password sign-in. Leave it unset for a public client.
settings.whereToFind: The user pool › App clients › the app client, Client secret (Show client secret).

settings.label: User pool domain
settings.meaning: The managed login (hosted UI) domain, such as auth.example.com or example.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com. Needed for social sign-in, code exchange, refresh and sign-out.
settings.whereToFind: The user pool › Branding › Domain: the Cognito domain, or your custom domain.

settings.label: AWS access key ID
settings.meaning: Signs the admin calls that read, create and delete users. Optional: without it the AWS SDK's default credential chain (an IAM role, AWS_PROFILE, ...) is used.
settings.whereToFind: IAM › Users › the app's user › Security credentials › Access keys, for a user allowed cognito-idp:AdminGetUser, ListUsers, AdminCreateUser, AdminDeleteUser and AdminSetUserPassword on the pool. Prefer an IAM role where the app runs on AWS.

settings.label: AWS secret access key
settings.meaning: The secret half of the AWS access key, set together with the access key ID.
settings.whereToFind: Shown once, when the access key is created in IAM.

operations.name: jwks.get
operations.purpose: Reads the user pool's public signing keys, from https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}/.well-known/jwks.json.

operations.name: auth.initiate
operations.purpose: Signs a user in with their username and password (InitiateAuth, AuthFlow USER_PASSWORD_AUTH), with SECRET_HASH for a confidential client. Unsigned JSON: X-Amz-Target AWSCognitoIdentityProviderService.InitiateAuth, Content-Type application/x-amz-json-1.1.

operations.name: tokens.exchange
operations.purpose: Exchanges an authorization code and its PKCE verifier for ID, access and refresh tokens, at the user pool domain's /oauth2/token (grant_type authorization_code).

operations.name: tokens.refresh
operations.purpose: Exchanges a refresh token for new ID and access tokens (and a new refresh token when rotation is on), at the user pool domain's /oauth2/token (grant_type refresh_token).

operations.name: tokens.revoke
operations.purpose: Revokes a refresh token and the access tokens issued with it, at the user pool domain's /oauth2/revoke.

operations.name: users.get
operations.purpose: Reads one user by username or sub (AdminGetUser, signed with AWS SigV4).

operations.name: users.list
operations.purpose: Finds users by one attribute, exactly (ListUsers with a Filter such as email = "a@example.com", signed with AWS SigV4).

operations.name: users.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user without sending Cognito's invitation (AdminCreateUser with MessageAction SUPPRESS, signed with AWS SigV4).

operations.name: users.setPassword
operations.purpose: Sets a user's permanent password (AdminSetUserPassword with Permanent true, signed with AWS SigV4).

operations.name: users.delete
operations.purpose: Deletes a user (AdminDeleteUser, signed with AWS SigV4).
